chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub al-Sarraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Christian woman whose husband died while he was a Christian, what is her waiting period (iddah)? He said, 'The waiting period of the free Muslim woman is four months and ten days.'

key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: the free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the iddah of a Christian woman if her husband dies?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the iddah of a free Christian woman whose husband dies while still a Christian is identical to that of a free Muslim woman, lasting four months and ten days. This ruling highlights the principle of *istihsan* (juridical preference) in Shia fiqh, where the status of the deceased husband's religion does not alter the widow's waiting period, distinguishing it from the iddah of a Muslim widow whose husband was Muslim. The consistency in duration underscores the uniformity of marital dissolution protocols across religious lines in this specific context.
